global_issues.title: Lawmakers advance China AI chip export curbs; Nvidia, AMD lobby Trump
global_issues.note: Politico and Benzinga (Sept 29) report Nvidia and AMD lobbying the White House and Commerce to keep China chip export provisions, tied to the AI OVERWATCH Act and Chip Security Act, out of the annual defense bill. Sen. Warren is pushing for a halt to Nvidia's advanced chip sales to China. The White House reportedly urged Congress to reject the restriction bill. The briefing's 'lawmakers plan new restrictions' wording is slightly loose. The restrictions are proposed provisions, not enacted, and the briefing doesn't mention the White House position or the defense bill vehicle. No change in the last 24h found that makes it outdated.

missing_major_news.title: Soft August PCE inflation print on Sept 30; S&P 500 closed -0.25% at 7,651.54 after erasing earlier gains; Nasdaq +0.24%
missing_major_news.impact: Broad-market and rate-sensitive names. The briefing mentions 'cooler inflation prints' only generically, with no PCE detail and no note of the late-session reversal. Nasdaq outperformed the S&P, which supports the tech leadership framing.

missing_major_news.title: 10-year Treasury yield rose about 4bp to ~5.30% and the 30-year to ~5.64% on Sept 30, despite the soft PCE. The S&P 500 had a losing September (-0.5%)
missing_major_news.impact: Raises discount-rate pressure on high-multiple holdings (NVDA, PLTR, CRWD, TSLA, MU). The briefing says yields are 'still rising' but gives no levels or quarter-end context.

missing_major_news.title: Strong tech and mega-cap momentum into quarter-end. Meta reportedly up about 29% in September on its Muse consumer AI agent launch, and Microsoft is having its best quarter since 1991
missing_major_news.impact: META is listed as 'DISTRIBUTION' with action=watch. That looks at odds with a month of roughly +29%. MSFT 'buy' is consistent with its strength. Both need a price check against the actual move, not just the stage label.

grok_report.summary: The lead issue (Nvidia and AMD lobbying against China chip curbs in the defense bill) is accurate and current. The briefing misses the PCE/yield/quarter-end context and leans on the chip-curb story as the main market driver. The META DISTRIBUTION label conflicts with its strong September, and the sector 'defensive rotation' framing is weakly supported. I could only verify MU's price, which is within about 0.4%; other quoted closes (TSM, NVDA, TSLA, PLTR, CRWD, AMZN, MSFT, AAPL) were not individually checked.
